# Translation policy

## Priority

1. Preserve GitHub Actions and Mona/exercise-toolkit behavior.
2. Preserve learner tasks, ordering, difficulty, and intentional defects.
3. Preserve technical meaning and repository-specific terminology.
4. Improve Korean readability only within those constraints.

Translate explanatory prose, headings, labels, and learner guidance when they
are not machine-checked. Do not translate paths, filenames, identifiers,
expressions, command flags, action names, code, frontmatter keys, workflow
inputs, checked keyphrases, or placeholders.

Keep the same level of certainty and obligation. Translate “must,” “should,” and
“may” distinctly. Do not add solutions, prerequisites, steps, links, or examples
that were not present. Preserve deliberately missing files and incomplete
starter content.

Use consistent Korean terminology from `terminology-ko.md`. On first use, retain
an English product or API term in parentheses when that prevents ambiguity.
Prefer concise instructional Korean and active voice.
